# Results — Study 632 (Crypto Cross-Sectional Momentum)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test
(Liu, Tsyvinski & Wu 2022, JF; Liu & Tsyvinski 2021, RFS) — **sort coins on last week's
return and last week's winners keep winning: cross-sectional momentum is the one return
factor crypto actually has** — rebuilt as a weekly quintile panel on a fixed 44-coin
top-cap universe (Binance spot 1w klines spliced with yfinance `-USD` backfills).
Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every
number. As-of **2026-06-28** (the last complete Monday-to-Sunday UTC week; the
in-progress week is dropped). Fingerprint `df8a5231ba1d`.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | Binance spot **1w klines** (public, keyless; weeks open Monday 00:00 UTC) + **yfinance `-USD`** daily closes used only to backfill pre-Binance-listing weeks |
| Panel | **495 weeks × 44 coins**, 2017-01-02 → 2026-06-22 open (9.5 years); strategy live from **2017-11-20** (first week with ≥ 10 eligible coins); average cross-section **34.9** coins |
| Delisted names | **11 of 44** pairs are delisted-from-Binance or dead — EOS, XMR, WAVES, OMG, NANO, MATIC, FTM, FTT, ANT, SRM, **LUNA (kept through its −100% death week; the Terra 2.0 relisting under the same symbol is truncated away)** |
| Signal | rank all eligible coins at the week-*t* close on their past *k*-week return (headline **k = 1**); Winners = top quintile, Losers = bottom quintile, equal-weight (`max(2, n//5)` names) |
| Execution / costs | **exactly one execution lag**: positions formed on week-*t* closes earn the week *t+1* close-to-close return; costs **one-way bps × traded NAV** (buys + sells each pay one leg, turnover measured); shorts pay **10 %/yr borrow** on short NAV |

> **Survivorship (named on the Signal axis).** The 11 delisted/dead pairs — including
> LUNA's −100 % week and FTT's −93 % week, which the losers leg *does* short and the
> winners leg *can* be long — soften the bias but do not remove it: the 33 *live* names
> are coins still top-cap in 2026, and pre-2019 casualties that never had a fetchable
> Binance USDT pair (BCC/BSV forks, XEM, BTG, most 2017 ICO tokens) are absent. The
> panel still tilts toward eventual winners, which flatters the *levels* (especially the
> winners leg and the market) more than the winners-minus-losers *spread*; we name it
> rather than pretend to fix it. One splice-week return per backfilled coin crosses the
> yfinance→Binance seam (same asset, same USD unit).

|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **1 (headline)** | 449 (2017-11-20) | **+164.1** | **+133.8 %** | **+3.56** | **1.12** | 55.0 | +113.2 (+3.30) |
| 2 | 448 | +135.4 | +101.8 % | +1.88 | 0.66 | 53.8 | +114.0 (+2.22) |

Context: the equal-weight market earns +148.0 bps/wk (HAC *t* = 1.90 — crypto beta alone

**The claim clears the bar on the real tape**: the 1-week sort — the claim exactly as

not a one-horizon artefact (*t* = 2.95 and 2.61 at *k* = 3, 4; *k* = 2 dips to 1.88).
This is the cross-sectional panel — distinct from the desk's
[251-crypto-reversal](../../251-crypto-reversal/) (short-horizon *reversal*, opposite
sign) and [222-altseason-rotation](../../222-altseason-rotation/) (two-asset
BTC-dominance rotation).

## Sub-periods (k = 1 WML) — the profile of a decaying, bull-loaded factor

| period | weeks | bps/wk | ann. | HAC *t* | hit % |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2017–2019 (early) | 111 | +194.6 | +173.4 % | +1.62 | 55.9 |
| 2020–2021 (bull) | 104 | **+371.6** | +571.0 % | **+3.80** | 63.5 |
| **2022 (bear)** | 52 | **+10.5** | +5.6 % | **+0.13** | 48.1 |
| 2023–2026 (late) | 182 | +70.8 | +44.5 % | +1.30 | 51.6 |

The full-sample *t* is carried by 2020–2021. Since 2023 the spread is positive but
sub-2 on its own (*t* = 1.30) — consistent with a real factor that has decayed as the
market institutionalised.

## Third axis — does it survive the 2022 bear? **Busted.**

Calendar 2022: **+10.5 bps/wk, HAC *t* = 0.13, hit 48.1 %** — statistically
indistinguishable from zero through the LUNA/FTX year. The tradable regime split
(lagged flag: BTC above/below its 30-week SMA at formation, applied to the next week —
no look-ahead) says the same thing:

| regime (lagged BTC > 30w SMA) | weeks | WML bps/wk | HAC *t* | Sharpe |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| bull | 243 | +255.8 | +3.51 | 1.47 |
| bear | 206 | +56.0 | +1.13 | 0.55 |

Welch *t* on the bull−bear difference = **+2.09**. Momentum in crypto is a
**bull-market factor**: in bear regimes it does not lose money, but it cannot certify
itself (*t* = 1.13), and in 2022 specifically it paid nothing.

## Costs — survives exchange-taker fees, dies at alt-spread slippage

Measured turnover: winners leg trades **1.48× NAV/week**, losers leg **1.60×** (the
sort replaces most of a quintile every week). Net = gross − one-way cost × traded NAV −
10 %/yr borrow on the short leg.

| one-way cost | WML net bps/wk | net ann. | HAC *t* | long-only WIN net − MKT (*t*) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 10 bps (BTC/ETH taker) | +114.1 | +80.7 % | **+2.47** | +98.4 bps/wk (+2.86) |
| 25 bps (liquid alts) | +67.8 | +42.3 % | +1.46 | +76.1 bps/wk (**+2.21**) |
| 50 bps (thin alts / 2018 era) | −9.3 | −4.7 % | −0.20 | +39.0 bps/wk (+1.13) |

At major-pair taker fees the long-short still clears *t* = 2; at realistic all-in
alt-coin slippage it drops below the bar, and at 50 bps it is dead. The **long-only
winners tilt** (no shorting, no borrow) is the more robust vehicle: it beats the
equal-weight market at *t* = 2.86 / 2.21 for 10 / 25 bps. Shorting thin alts at size is
partly aspirational anyway (borrow is scarce exactly when losers crash) — a second,
independent reason the two-legged spread is fragile.

## Placebo — random ranks, averaged over 20 seeds

Replacing the formation ranks with i.i.d. noise (same eligibility, same quintile sizes,
same lag) pays **+7.2 ± 36.4 bps/wk** across 20 seeds, mean HAC *t* = **+0.20**. The
machinery does not pay a shuffled signal.

## Synthetic control — the engine is faithful *(machinery proof only, never evidence)*

| planted 1-week idiosyncratic momentum | WML bps/wk | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| ρ = 0 (null) | −39.2 | −1.09 |
| ρ = 0.10 (planted) | +396.7 | **+11.14** |

The quintile detector stays quiet on a null crypto-vol panel and lights up on a planted
AR(1) continuation — the real-tape *t* = 3.56 is not a construction artefact.

## Verdict

- **Signal — REAL.** Last week's winners keep winning: **+164 bps/week** long-short
  (ann. ≈ +134 %), **HAC *t* = 3.56**, Sharpe 1.12, robust across 3- and 4-week
  formations (*t* = 2.95, 2.61) and against a 20-seed random-rank placebo (~0). Clears
  the desk's *t* ≥ 2 bar on the real tape. Carries a named **survivorship** caveat —
  softened by 11 delisted/dead pairs (LUNA's death week included) but not removed.
- **Tradability — FRAGILE.** Weekly quintiles churn ~1.5× NAV per leg per week: net of
  10 bps one-way the spread still clears the bar (*t* = 2.47), at 25 bps it is *t* =
  1.46, at 50 bps it is gone. The factor is **regime-dependent** (bull *t* = 3.51 vs
  bear 1.13) and **decayed** (2023–2026 *t* = 1.30 alone). The long-only winners tilt
  survives 25 bps (*t* = 2.21) — real but conditional, not INVESTABLE.
- **"Does it survive the 2022 bear?" — BUSTED.** 2022: +10.5 bps/wk, *t* = 0.13, hit
  48.1 %. Bear-regime weeks overall: *t* = 1.13, with a Welch *t* = 2.09 bull-bear gap.
  Crypto momentum is a bull-market factor; it went silent exactly when a hedge was
  wanted.
